title: "V: Various"
description: "ATC group V for modellers: the catch-all letter, effective half-life for radiopharmaceuticals, and notes held at V03, V08 and V10."
date: "2026-02-08"

ATC group V is the catch-all letter of the classification [@whoccATCDDDIndex2026].
The notes below cover three of its nine level 2 codes: therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals, reversal agents and contrast media.

In 2002 Anton Bom and colleagues at Organon described a cyclodextrin that reverses rocuronium block by encapsulating the relaxant itself rather than acting on a receptor [@bomNovelConceptReversing2002].

| Level 2 code | Description | In plain terms | Current standard |
| ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| V01 | Allergens | extracts for allergy testing and desensitisation | Grass pollen allergen extract (V01AA02) / house dust mite allergen extract (V01AA03) |
| [V03](v03_all-other-therapeutic-products/) | All other therapeutic products | catch-all: antidotes, chelators, medical gases | Naloxone (V03AB15) / acetylcysteine (V03AB23) |
| V04 | Diagnostic agents |  | Tuberculin (V04CF01) / 13C-urea (V04CX05) |
| V06 | General nutrients |  | No drug-level standard: enteral and parenteral nutrition products are classified at group level only (V06A, V06B, V06C, V06DA, V06DB, V06DD, V06DE, V06DF, V06DX carry no level 5 substances). The only level 5 entries in the whole group are glucose (V06DC01) and fructose (V06DC02). |
| V07 | All other non-therapeutic products | non-medicines: dressings, solvents, disinfectants, cosmetics | No drug-level standard and no level 5 codes anywhere in the group: every subgroup stops at level 4, e.g. solvents and diluting agents (V07AB), blood transfusion auxiliary products (V07AC), technical disinfectants (V07AV). |
| [V08](v08_contrast-media/) | Contrast media | injected agents that make scans visible | Iohexol (V08AB02) / gadobutrol (V08CA09) |
| V09 | Diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals | radioactive tracers injected to image the body | Fludeoxyglucose (18F) (V09IX04) / technetium (99mTc) medronic acid (V09BA02) |
| [V10](v10_therapeutic-radiopharmaceuticals/) | Therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals | radioactive drugs given to treat disease | Sodium iodide (131I) (V10XA01) / lutetium (177Lu) vipivotide tetraxetan (V10XX05) |
| V20 | Surgical dressings |  | No drug-level standard: V20 has no subdivisions at all. The classification stops at the level 2 group code V20 (surgical dressings), with no level 3, 4 or 5 entries. |

## Modelling notes

**Endpoint.**
For therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals the driver is a physical quantity, the **absorbed dose** in Gy to tumour and organs at risk, reconstructed from serial post-infusion imaging rather than from a plasma concentration-time curve [@hebertAbsorbedDoseResponse2024].
In ^177^Lu-PSMA-617 therapy the lesion dose-response relationship is real but only moderate, Spearman rho about -0.3 [@grkovskiLesionAbsorbedDose2025].

**Decay is not clearance (V09, V10).**
Imaging measures activity, which falls by radioactive decay and by biological clearance together, so what is fitted is an effective half-life [@oliveiraAnalysisResidenceTime2022].
With few imaging time points the fit is unstable, and population fitting stabilises the time-integrated activity [@hardiansyahPopulationBasedMethod2021].
